subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — Orchid Systems (mixed GPU families, burst & overage terms)
messages:
From: Elaine Wong <elaine.wong@orchidsys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2028-03-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — Orchid Systems (mix & billing)

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week. We’re ready to move forward with a 12-month dedicated capacity commitment but have a few non-standard asks that procurement needs cleared before legal/finance will sign:

- Capacity mix: initial pool of 8x H100-equivalent and 4x H200-equivalent nodes. We will run throughput-heavy batch jobs most nights but need low-latency inference during daytime.
- Burst window: ability to burst an additional ~20% H100-equivalent capacity for a 6-week ramp (anticipated product launch), with transparent overage billing during that window.
- Overage pricing: procurement is requesting a capped overage rate that’s below standard list. They want a blended overage cap rather than unbounded per-minute billing.
- Pricing: they’re asking for a 20% enterprise discount on committed spend for year 1 (12-month commit) given the volume and a marketing partnership.
- Reservation hold: they’d like Redwood to hold the proposed capacity and not reassign until procurement completes (target close by 2028-03-10).

I’ve attached our usage spreadsheet and last quarter’s utilization to help size the pool. Can your team approve the above exceptions or propose alternatives? Procurement needs a go/no-go by 2028-03-10 to avoid delaying our launch.

Thanks — happy to hop on a call.

Regards,
Elaine Wong
Head of Infrastructure
Orchid Systems
(415) 555-0192
Attachments: orchid_capacity_needs.xlsx, orchid_usage_history.csv
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com, rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com

Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — Orchid Systems (need exec signoff on mixed GPU & billing exceptions)

Forwarding Orchid’s request — procurement will not sign without exec approval on three items. Summary and asks below. Please see Elaine’s original email quoted after my note.

Summary of asks from Orchid Systems (high priority):
1) Mixed-GPU pool: allow initial mix of 8 H100 + 4 H200 equivalents on a single Dedicated commitment (they want the ability to move workload between families during the first 3 months while they tune).
2) Burst window: allow up to ~20% additional H100-equivalent for a 6-week burst (product launch), billed as overage but subject to a negotiated cap.
3) Discount/terms: 20% off committed list price for year 1 on a 12-month term; reservation hold while procurement finalizes (request hold until 2028-03-31).

Proposed commercial alternative (my suggested starting point):
- Approve mixed-GPU pilot for 90 days with an agreed migration plan and runbook.
- Approve a capped overage structure for the 6-week burst: propose cap $5.00 / hr per H100-equivalent and $1.75 / hr per H200-equivalent (these are negotiable if Finance or Pricing want different bands).
- Offer an 18% committed-spend discount for year 1 with a performance-based kicker (additional 2% credit if usage > 75% of committed capacity for three consecutive months).
- Place a reservation hold for 26 business days (through 2028-03-31) contingent on an executed non-binding term sheet.

Asks to the group:
- Karthik / Lauren — can you weigh in on operational feasibility and risk (fallback if H100 availability constrained)?
- Finance / Legal — Vivek / Rachel — can we approve the proposed overage caps and the 18% discount (or advise counter) as an exec exception?

Timing: procurement wants a decision by 2028-03-10. If we can get a clear approval by EOD 2028-03-06, I can present a final term sheet to Orchid and expedite DocuSign.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks Marissa — quick clarifying Qs from the serving/runtime side before we lock numbers:
1) Blended vs. discrete billing: do we want a blended unit price for the mixed pool (single hourly rate for the committed pool) or separate pricing by family (H100 vs H200) and then blended for overage? Blended is simpler operationally but hides unit economics.
2) Burst enforcement: how strict do we need the 6-week burst window to be? Can we offer a time-boxed burst with a hard end-date and an automated reversion to baseline to protect capacity planning?
3) Availability fallback: if H100 supply is constrained, are we comfortable automatically substituting with H200-capable nodes with a small performance SLA note to the customer?

Operationally I think we can support a 90-day mixed pilot and a 6-week timed burst if we: (a) create a runbook (capacity_runbook.xlsx), (b) add an automated cap enforcement, and (c) document substitution rules. Numbers: I’m + on the proposed overage caps as a starting point but would prefer the H100 cap to be $5.25/hr and H200 at $1.90/hr to reflect supply differentials unless Finance prefers alternate bands.

If Finance/legal are okay with a conditional exec exception I’ll prepare the operational SOW addendum.

— Karthik
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.inference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com, rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2028-03-06T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — Orchid Systems (need exec signoff on mixed GPU & billing exceptions)

I’ve reviewed the ask and operational impact. High-level: I’m comfortable approving a controlled mixed-GPU pilot and a time-bound burst with the following guardrails:

- Mixed pilot: approve 90-day mixed deployment (8 H100 + 4 H200). Require a migration/runbook and a weekly sync with our SREs to monitor perf. If H100 supply issues arise, we automatically substitute with H200 only with a 48h notice to the customer and a documented performance caveat.
- Reservation hold: approve hold through 2028-03-31 contingent on a signed non-binding term sheet and receipt of their PO.
- Burst: approve the 6-week timed burst window but suggest a slightly higher H100 cap to protect unit economics: $5.25/hr for H100, $1.90/hr for H200 during overage.
- Discount: I cannot approve a straight 20% off list. I will approve up to 15% committed discount today. If Sales is willing to accept an adoption-based kicker (additional credits up to 3% if usage thresholds met), we can bridge the gap. Final discount needs Finance signoff.

Vivek/Rachel: please confirm whether you can sign the 15% + adoption kicker structure. If Finance prefers a single blended cap instead of family-specific overage caps, state that and we’ll re-price.

Lauren
Director, Customer Success

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity request — Orchid Systems (final exec approval)

Thanks all — I reviewed the commercial impact and risk. After discussion with Pricing, Legal, and Revenue Ops, we can approve the following executive exceptions for Orchid Systems DEAL-98432 with conditions:

Approved exceptions (final):
- Mixed-GPU pilot: 8x H100 + 4x H200 for an initial 90-day period. Require an SOW addendum specifying migration plan and a weekly operational checkpoint.
- Reservation hold: hold proposed nodes until 2028-03-31, conditional on Orchid signing a non-binding term sheet and delivering a PO by that date.
- Burst: allow a 6-week timed burst window. Overage caps approved at $5.00/hr per H100-equivalent and $1.75/hr per H200-equivalent for the burst period. We’ll enforce caps with automated billing rules and post-burst reconciliation.
- Discount: approve a 17% committed-spend discount for year 1 (compromise between Sales/Customer ask and our headroom). Additionally, include a performance credit of up to 3% if Orchid sustains >75% utilization of committed capacity for three consecutive months within the first 6 months.

Conditions / next steps:
1) Legal (Rachel) to draft an SOW addendum and revised term sheet; Sales to publish a one-page non-binding term sheet for Orchid this week.
2) Marissa — please update HubSpot (link above) and attach the capacity_runbook.xlsx and the proposed SOW addendum.
3) We need a signed PO and the DocuSign addendum by 2028-03-31 to maintain the reservation hold.
4) Finance will track expected margin impact; any top-line variance > 12% against forecast will require Exec notification.

I will issue a formal approval memo after Legal provides the addendum language. Marissa, proceed to share these terms with Orchid and request the PO.

— Vivek
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
